releases.body:
Auto Ontology 1.3.0 is published to the public NGC Catalog. These notes cover everything since 1.1.0 (October 2026), including the changes that first shipped in 1.2.0.

## 🚀 ReAct: a new text-to-SQL agent

1.3.0 replaces the LangGraph text-to-SQL implementation with a single **ReAct** agent. The change brings major improvements in runtime speed, token efficiency and output accuracy (#488).

**Benchmark highlights (BEAVER, Claude Opus 5.5):**
- **Accuracy:** up to **20%** higher
- **Token consumption:** **4x** lower overall
- **Cache hit rate:** **82%** of tokens served from cache
- **Latency and volume:** **2x** fewer model calls and much shorter runtimes

When this release was prepared, Auto Ontology ranked **first on [BEAVER](https://beaverbench.github.io/#leaderboard)**, and **first on both BIRD-Interact-A and BIRD-Interact-C** ([BIRD-Interact](https://bird-interact.github.io/)) (#521).

**How it works**
- **One loop.** The model calls tools until it submits an answer. It alone decides what to search, what to run and when it is done. The loop only enforces the budget, refuses repeated calls, and turns a submission into an answer once it runs cleanly (#488).

# Auto Ontology Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need context to answer accurately: what each business concept means, where it lives, how it connects, how to calculate it, where it comes from, and whether to trust it. An ontology holds that context: a shared, governed map from the concepts people ask about to the data behind them. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that ontology automatically from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own, and [Apache Ossie](https://ossie.apache.org/) keeps it portable. Auto Ontology leads on the [BIRD-Interact](https://bird-interact.github.io/) and [BEAVER](https://beaverbench.github.io/#leaderboard) benchmarks, which test the accuracy of text-to-SQL analytics question answering in interactive flows with ambiguous user inputs and on large-scale, messy databases. It enables developers to: - **Discover:** generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs. - **Ground:** give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems. - **Validate:** test a draft with real questions before experts certify it; check generated queries against the catalog and the definitions retrieval surfaced; return the SQL and steps with every answer. - **Expose:** serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. - **Learn:** fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with use. An ontology matters most when: - questions are varied, open-ended, and ambiguous; - data spans many disparate sources with overlapping or conflicting definitions; - meanings must be reused and governed across runs, teams, and agents; - the model or its context budget can't hold the full documentation; - users ask in business terms and need routing to the right source and grain. With one well-modeled source and a fixed set of questions, direct SQL may be enough. ## Quickstart This runs Auto Ontology with Docker Compose against Wide World Importers, Microsoft's sample sales database. You need Docker with Compose v2, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and an NVIDIA API key (`nvapi-...`) from [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com). 1. Clone the repository and create `.env`: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git && cd auto-ontology cp .env.example .env ``` Then set these values in `.env`: ```dotenv DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY=nvapi-... AUTH_SECRET= APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 POSTGRES_PASSWORD= CONNECTION_STRINGS=postgresql://postgres:@postgres:5432/wideworldimporters AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD= PGADMIN_PASSWORD= ``` Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin, and the web app on the host, so replace each default password before you start it. `.env.example` also sets an API key per model role: replace each `nvapi-your-api-key-here` with your key, or delete those lines so they fall back to `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. 2. Start Postgres and load the sample database. The seed script lives in auto-ontology-eval; pass it the Postgres password you set: ```bash docker compose up -d --wait postgres git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval.git ../auto-ontology-eval (cd ../auto-ontology-eval && uv sync && cp .env.example .env && \ POSTGRES_PASSWORD='' \ uv run python scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py --database-name wideworldimporters --drop) ``` 3. Build and start the rest of the stack: ```bash docker compose up -d --build ``` 4. Open and sign in with `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `.env`. Go to **Settings → Semantic Compilation** and turn it on. Ingestion runs at startup; compilation starts immediately and reports **Semantic compilation is ready** when it finishes. 5. Ask a question in **Chat**: > What was revenue for the USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania > in June 2015? The agent resolves *revenue*, *product*, and *state* to terms in the ontology, follows their relationships to the joins it needs, and runs the query. The answer comes back with its SQL and the steps that produced it, so you can check the result against the source: ```text Answer: Revenue for USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in June 2015 was $588.80, from 3 invoice lines. SQL: SELECT SUM(il.extendedprice) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS invoice_lines FROM sales.invoicelines il JOIN sales.invoices i ON il.invoiceid = i.invoiceid JOIN warehouse.stockitems si ON il.stockitemid = si.stockitemid JOIN sales.customers c ON i.customerid = c.customerid JOIN application.cities ct ON c.deliverycityid = ct.cityid JOIN application.stateprovinces sp ON ct.stateprovinceid = sp.stateprovinceid WHERE si.stockitemname = 'USB food flash drive - sushi roll' AND sp.stateprovincename = 'Pennsylvania' AND i.invoicedate >= '2015-06-01' AND i.invoicedate < '2015-07-01' Steps: Resolved terms: Invoice Line (revenue), Stock Item, State Province, Invoice Joined: invoice line -> invoice -> customer -> city -> state province Validated the filter values against the data, then executed ``` 6. Ask something the data can't answer. Wide World Importers has no advertising data, so a question about ad spend has nothing to resolve against. An agent connected through [MCP](#mcp-server) checks answerability first and asks you to clarify: ```text You: What was return on ad spend for the sushi roll flash drive in June 2015? Agent: check_answerable -> coverage 0.5; no term covers "ad spend" Agent: I can find revenue for that product, but this data has no advertising spend, so I can't compute return on ad spend. Do you want June 2015 revenue instead, or is ad spend tracked in another source I should connect? ``` If the UI loads without its left navigation after a restart, the browser is holding a stale session cookie. Clear site data for `localhost:3000` and sign in again. For other setup failures, see the [setup skill's troubleshooting guide](./skills/nvidia-ontology-setup/references/troubleshooting.md). ## How it works Auto Ontology works in two stages: it generates an ontology that people certify, and the agent answers questions from it. The ontology answers six questions, each with its own element: | Question | Element | In Auto Ontology | | ------------------------ | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | What does it mean? | Concept | A term, such as *Customer* or *Invoice Line*, with a description and synonyms | | Where is it? | Mapping | Column attributes tie each term to the tables and columns that hold it | | What's connected? | Relationship | Joins between tables, including bridge tables: declared keys, plus inferred links confirmed against the data | | How do I calculate it? | Metric | SQL attributes: reviewed SQL under a term, such as a margin, reused so answers compute each measure the same way | | Where does it come from? | Lineage | Each term and attribute links to its source tables and columns, and each answer returns its SQL | | Should I use it? | Certification | Experts certify names, descriptions, and attributes, and certified elements are marked as reviewed | **Generate:** the ingestion service builds a first draft from the source databases, and people refine it. Semantic compilation starts once you turn it on in **Settings → Semantic Compilation**. - **Catalog ingest:** read tables, columns, keys, views, and query history; tag PII if you turn on PII detection; embed tables and columns in pgvector. - **Per table:** profile values with SQL. A model finds foreign key candidates and junction tables, writes column descriptions, and names the terms. - **Across tables:** group copies of a schema into term families, and link foreign keys to the terms they reference, keeping an inferred link only when the data confirms it. A model attaches foreign key columns left unlinked, suggests SQL attributes from query history and for bridge tables, and describes each column attribute. - **Output:** the ontology in Postgres with embeddings in pgvector, which you can import or export as Ossie YAML. - **Certify:** test the draft with real questions in Chat, or with `check_answerable` and `ask_question` over MCP. Refine terms, descriptions, and SQL attributes in the UI or through the API, and certify them once they're correct. Edits are re-embedded right away, and the next compilation keeps them, except which semantic foreign key each join uses, which every compilation re-selects. The [Generate tool flow](./docs/architecture.md#generate-an-ontology) shows which steps call a model and which are SQL or rules. The result is a semantic graph you can explore in the UI. In this example, one compilation of Wide World Importers produced 31 terms; selecting **Order** shows its description, related terms, mapped columns, and SQL attributes:

**Answer:** the reasoning model answers each question in a loop, choosing one tool at a time: - **`retrieve`:** search the semantic layer by meaning and by name for business concepts, column meanings, and named calculations. Results come back as tables and columns with their descriptions and stored values, definitions with their SQL, and join paths. The model searches again whenever something is missing. - **`run_sql`:** look at stored values or test a draft. Before the query runs, table and column names are checked against the catalog, and tables against what `retrieve` showed. - **`submit`:** give the final query and an explanation. The query is checked and run, and an error goes back to the model to fix. A question about the data itself, such as which tables exist or what a term means, is answered in words: `retrieve` looks it up with `purpose=information`, and `submit` returns the answer without SQL. - **Result:** the answer comes back with its SQL and the steps it took, and a chart in Chat. No tool calls a language model except `predict`, which answers predictive questions when `KUMO_RFM_API_URL` is set; see [Predictions](#predictions). If the model reaches its tool-call limit without an accepted query, the agent reports that the question can't be answered from this data. The [Answer tool flow](./docs/architecture.md#answer-a-question) shows the loop, its tools, and its limits. In Chat, each answer shows its SQL, and you can view the rows, download them as CSV, or read them as a chart:

Auto Ontology

Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need context to answer accurately: what each business concept means, where it lives, how it connects, how to calculate it, where it comes from, and whether to trust it. An ontology holds that context: a shared, governed map from the concepts people ask about to the data behind them. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that ontology automatically from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own, and Apache Ossie keeps it portable.

Auto Ontology leads on the BIRD-Interact and BEAVER benchmarks, which test the accuracy of text-to-SQL analytics question answering in interactive flows with ambiguous user inputs and on large-scale, messy databases.

It enables developers to:

  • Discover: generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs.
  • Ground: give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems.
  • Validate: test a draft with real questions before experts certify it; check generated queries against the catalog and the definitions retrieval surfaced; return the SQL and steps with every answer.
  • Expose: serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API.
  • Learn: fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with use.

An ontology matters most when:

  • questions are varied, open-ended, and ambiguous;
  • data spans many disparate sources with overlapping or conflicting definitions;
  • meanings must be reused and governed across runs, teams, and agents;
  • the model or its context budget can't hold the full documentation;
  • users ask in business terms and need routing to the right source and grain.

With one well-modeled source and a fixed set of questions, direct SQL may be enough.

Quickstart

This runs Auto Ontology with Docker Compose against Wide World Importers, Microsoft's sample sales database. You need Docker with Compose v2, uv, and an NVIDIA API key (nvapi-...) from build.nvidia.com.

  1. Clone the repository and create .env:

    git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git && cd auto-ontology
cp .env.example .env

    Then set these values in .env:

    DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY=nvapi-...
AUTH_SECRET=<a long random string, e.g. from openssl rand -base64 32>
APP_URL=http://localhost:3000
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<a new password>
CONNECTION_STRINGS=postgresql://postgres:<the same password>@postgres:5432/wideworldimporters
AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<a new password>
PGADMIN_PASSWORD=<a new password>

    Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin, and the web app on the host, so replace each default password before you start it. .env.example also sets an API key per model role: replace each nvapi-your-api-key-here with your key, or delete those lines so they fall back to DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY.

  2. Start Postgres and load the sample database. The seed script lives in auto-ontology-eval; pass it the Postgres password you set:

    docker compose up -d --wait postgres
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval.git ../auto-ontology-eval
(cd ../auto-ontology-eval && uv sync && cp .env.example .env && \
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD='<the same password>' \
  uv run python scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py --database-name wideworldimporters --drop)

  3. Build and start the rest of the stack:

    docker compose up -d --build

  4. Open http://localhost:3000 and sign in with AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_EMAIL and AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env. Go to Settings → Semantic Compilation and turn it on. Ingestion runs at startup; compilation starts immediately and reports Semantic compilation is ready when it finishes.

  5. Ask a question in Chat:

    What was revenue for the USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in June 2015?

    The agent resolves revenue, product, and state to terms in the ontology, follows their relationships to the joins it needs, and runs the query. The answer comes back with its SQL and the steps that produced it, so you can check the result against the source:

    Answer:  Revenue for USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in
         June 2015 was $588.80, from 3 invoice lines.

SQL:     SELECT SUM(il.extendedprice) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS invoice_lines
         FROM sales.invoicelines il
         JOIN sales.invoices i             ON il.invoiceid = i.invoiceid
         JOIN warehouse.stockitems si      ON il.stockitemid = si.stockitemid
         JOIN sales.customers c            ON i.customerid = c.customerid
         JOIN application.cities ct        ON c.deliverycityid = ct.cityid
         JOIN application.stateprovinces sp ON ct.stateprovinceid = sp.stateprovinceid
         WHERE si.stockitemname = 'USB food flash drive - sushi roll'
           AND sp.stateprovincename = 'Pennsylvania'
           AND i.invoicedate >= '2015-06-01' AND i.invoicedate < '2015-07-01'

Steps:   Resolved terms: Invoice Line (revenue), Stock Item, State Province, Invoice
         Joined: invoice line -> invoice -> customer -> city -> state province
         Validated the filter values against the data, then executed

  6. Ask something the data can't answer. Wide World Importers has no advertising data, so a question about ad spend has nothing to resolve against. An agent connected through MCP checks answerability first and asks you to clarify:

    You:    What was return on ad spend for the sushi roll flash drive in June 2015?
Agent:  check_answerable -> coverage 0.5; no term covers "ad spend"
Agent:  I can find revenue for that product, but this data has no
        advertising spend, so I can't compute return on ad spend. Do you
        want June 2015 revenue instead, or is ad spend tracked in another
        source I should connect?

If the UI loads without its left navigation after a restart, the browser is holding a stale session cookie. Clear site data for localhost:3000 and sign in again. For other setup failures, see the setup skill's troubleshooting guide.

How it works

Auto Ontology works in two stages: it generates an ontology that people certify, and the agent answers questions from it.

The ontology answers six questions, each with its own element:

Question Element In Auto Ontology
What does it mean? Concept A term, such as Customer or Invoice Line, with a description and synonyms
Where is it? Mapping Column attributes tie each term to the tables and columns that hold it
What's connected? Relationship Joins between tables, including bridge tables: declared keys, plus inferred links confirmed against the data
How do I calculate it? Metric SQL attributes: reviewed SQL under a term, such as a margin, reused so answers compute each measure the same way
Where does it come from? Lineage Each term and attribute links to its source tables and columns, and each answer returns its SQL
Should I use it? Certification Experts certify names, descriptions, and attributes, and certified elements are marked as reviewed

Generate: the ingestion service builds a first draft from the source databases, and people refine it. Semantic compilation starts once you turn it on in Settings → Semantic Compilation.

  • Catalog ingest: read tables, columns, keys, views, and query history; tag PII if you turn on PII detection; embed tables and columns in pgvector.
  • Per table: profile values with SQL. A model finds foreign key candidates and junction tables, writes column descriptions, and names the terms.
  • Across tables: group copies of a schema into term families, and link foreign keys to the terms they reference, keeping an inferred link only when the data confirms it. A model attaches foreign key columns left unlinked, suggests SQL attributes from query history and for bridge tables, and describes each column attribute.
  • Output: the ontology in Postgres with embeddings in pgvector, which you can import or export as Ossie YAML.
  • Certify: test the draft with real questions in Chat, or with check_answerable and ask_question over MCP. Refine terms, descriptions, and SQL attributes in the UI or through the API, and certify them once they're correct. Edits are re-embedded right away, and the next compilation keeps them, except which semantic foreign key each join uses, which every compilation re-selects.

The Generate tool flow shows which steps call a model and which are SQL or rules.

The result is a semantic graph you can explore in the UI. In this example, one compilation of Wide World Importers produced 31 terms; selecting Order shows its description, related terms, mapped columns, and SQL attributes:

Answer: the reasoning model answers each question in a loop, choosing one tool at a time:

  • retrieve: search the semantic layer by meaning and by name for business concepts, column meanings, and named calculations. Results come back as tables and columns with their descriptions and stored values, definitions with their SQL, and join paths. The model searches again whenever something is missing.
  • run_sql: look at stored values or test a draft. Before the query runs, table and column names are checked against the catalog, and tables against what retrieve showed.
  • submit: give the final query and an explanation. The query is checked and run, and an error goes back to the model to fix. A question about the data itself, such as which tables exist or what a term means, is answered in words: retrieve looks it up with purpose=information, and submit returns the answer without SQL.
  • Result: the answer comes back with its SQL and the steps it took, and a chart in Chat.

No tool calls a language model except predict, which answers predictive questions when KUMO_RFM_API_URL is set; see Predictions. If the model reaches its tool-call limit without an accepted query, the agent reports that the question can't be answered from this data. The Answer tool flow shows the loop, its tools, and its limits.

In Chat, each answer shows its SQL, and you can view the rows, download them as CSV, or read them as a chart:

Auto Ontology is compatible with Apache Ossie, the open standard for exchanging semantic models. Ossie includes a converter for Auto Ontology, which Auto Ontology uses to import and export model definitions as Ossie YAML. Use Settings → Import / Export, or POST /api/model/import and POST /api/model/export.

Use it from your agent

MCP server

The MCP server gives any MCP client read-only tools over the ontology. Each user signs in through Auto Ontology, and every call runs with that user's permissions.

Job Tools
Readiness check_readiness: can this deployment answer anything at all
Terms search_terms, get_term, get_term_columns, get_term_sql_attributes, get_sql_attribute, describe_table
Answerability check_answerable: does the ontology cover this question
Questions ask_question: the answer, the SQL, and the rows

Run the server against your deployment:

AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 \
  uvx --from "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git#subdirectory=mcp" auto-ontology-mcp

Cursor (~/.cursor/mcp.json):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "auto-ontology": { "url": "http://localhost:3003/mcp" }
  }
}

Claude Desktop (claude_desktop_config.json), bridged with mcp-remote:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "auto-ontology": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["mcp-remote", "http://localhost:3003/mcp"]
    }
  }
}

Restart the client after editing its config, then sign in when it prompts. Sign-in, configuration, and troubleshooting are in docs/mcp.md.

Agent skills

Three skills teach a coding agent to work with Auto Ontology. Start at AGENTS.md.

Skill Covers
nvidia-ontology-setup Install, connect sources, compile, prove readiness
nvidia-ontology-management Inspect, model, certify, import/export, and publish
nvidia-ontology-query Ask questions and validate the SQL, rows, and answer

REST API

Ask a question with POST /api/chat/completions on the web app's origin. Mint an API token under the user menu → API Tokens. The response is a server-sent event stream: a result event carries the answer, and data: [DONE] ends the stream.

curl -N http://localhost:3000/api/chat/completions \
  -H "x-api-key: $AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"question": "How many orders shipped last week?"}'
import json
import os

import requests

response = requests.post(
    "http://localhost:3000/api/chat/completions",
    headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_TOKEN"]},
    json={"question": "How many orders shipped last week?"},
    stream=True,
    timeout=900,
)
response.raise_for_status()

for line in response.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True):
    if not line or not line.startswith("data:"):
        continue
    payload = line.removeprefix("data:").strip()
    if payload == "[DONE]":
        break
    event = json.loads(payload)
    if event["type"] == "result":
        print(event["answer"]["response"])
        print(event["answer"]["sql_code"])
    elif event["type"] == "error":
        raise RuntimeError(event["message"])

Event types, multi-turn conversations, and the gateway trust boundary are in docs/conversation-api.md. Every other operation is in the OpenAPI spec.

Connectors, models, and predictions

Sources

Auto Ontology connects to eleven engines:

  • PostgreSQL
  • MySQL
  • Databricks
  • Snowflake
  • ClickHouse
  • Trino
  • Google BigQuery
  • Apache Kyuubi
  • HeavyDB
  • DuckDB
  • SQLite

Add connections under Settings → Connections, or list them in CONNECTION_STRINGS. DuckDB and SQLite are connection-string only. See docs/connections.md for URL schemes, scoping, and credential storage.

Models

Auto Ontology uses four model roles. With an nvapi- key, each defaults to an NVIDIA NIM on build.nvidia.com:

Role Default model What it does
REASONING nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b Runs the answering agent and check_answerable, builds the ontology, and detects PII
NON_REASONING nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b Rewrites follow-up questions, plans charts, writes PQL for predictions, and runs the quick steps of interactive analysis
EMBED nvidia/nemotron-3.5-embed-1b Indexes tables, columns, terms, and SQL attributes in pgvector, and matches each question to them
RERANK nvidia/nemotron-3.5-rerank-8b Picks the term that owns each bridge-table SQL attribute during compilation; not used to answer questions

To use self-hosted NIM or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set <ROLE>_ENDPOINT, <ROLE>_API_KEY, and <ROLE>_MODEL. Any field you leave unset falls back to DEFAULT_MODELS_<FIELD>, so the simplest setup fills in DEFAULT_MODELS_* and overrides only what differs; *_API_KEY also falls back to the legacy NVIDIA_API_KEY. Use models that support structured output, and keep the embedding model the same for ingestion and queries. .env.example documents every variable.

Predictions

Set KUMO_RFM_API_URL (and KUMO_RFM_API_KEY if your endpoint requires one) and the agent routes predictive questions to KumoRFM. KumoRFM is a hosted service: to answer, the agent uploads the connected tables to it, capped by KUMO_MAX_TABLES (20 by default) and KUMO_MAX_ROWS_PER_TABLE (unlimited unless set). Review what that sends, and complete your organization's data review, before you enable it.

Benchmarks

To run a text-to-SQL benchmark such as BIRD, refer to auto-ontology-eval, which scores the same model with and without the ontology on NeMo Gym.

Contributing

We welcome contributions: bug fixes, connectors, documentation, and examples. Please read the Contributing Guidelines before submitting pull requests.

To integrate an agent platform, application, or storage provider with Auto Ontology, open an integration request.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Auto Ontology is a Python framework designed to build semantic reasoning layers. It leverages graph-based structures to enhance data interpretation and context retrieval. The tool enables deterministic query generation for more reliable data interactions. It provides explainable AI capabilities for LLM and agent workflows. This significantly improves the transparency and accuracy of complex AI systems.
keyFeatures: Semantic reasoning: builds graph-based layers to improve data interpretation and context.
Deterministic querying: enables reliable and predictable query generation over structured data.
Explainable AI: provides transparency into the reasoning processes of LLM workflows.
Graph structures: utilizes knowledge graphs to represent complex semantic relationships.
Python framework: offers a comprehensive set of tools integrated into the Python ecosystem.

useCases.title: Build reasoning layers
useCases.description: Implement semantic graphs to improve the context retrieval of AI agents.

useCases.title: Generate reliable queries
useCases.description: Use deterministic methods to query complex datasets with high accuracy.

useCases.title: Enhance LLM workflows
useCases.description: Add explainable reasoning capabilities to large language model applications.

useCases.title: Improve data context
useCases.description: Structure unstructured data into semantic graphs for better understanding.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Data scientists and AI engineers building complex, reasoning-driven LLM applications. It is particularly valuable for projects requiring high accuracy and explainability. Familiarity with Python, knowledge graphs, and semantic data is highly recommended.
